parent_theme: Computational complexity of curing the sign problem
canonical_title: Extending NP-completeness of sign-problem curing to 2-local Hamiltonians
canonical_statement: Can the NP-completeness of finding curing transformations — proven for 3-local Hamiltonians under tensor products of single-qubit Clifford gates and for 6-local Hamiltonians under general single-qubit orthogonal rotations — be extended to 2-local Hamiltonians?
scope: The locality of the hardness constructions for the curing decision problem: whether the known NP-completeness results (3-local under single-qubit Clifford transformations; 6-local under single-qubit orthogonal transformations) can be reduced to 2-local building blocks, as the source paper explicitly poses as an open question.

source_support.exact_excerpt: Also, since our NP-completeness proof involved 333 and 666-local Hamiltonians, it is interesting to try to reduce it to 222-local building blocks.

aliases: Locality reduction for computational stoquasticity hardness
verification_plan: A submitted answer must settle the complexity of the curing decision problem at locality 2 under the paper's stated single-qubit transformation classes: either an NP-hardness/NP-completeness proof for 2-local Hamiltonians via an explicit rigorous reduction, or a polynomial-time algorithm with correctness proof showing the 2-local case is tractable, or a rigorous barrier/conditional result. It passes if the argument is mathematically rigorous, uses 2-local Hamiltonians throughout (not higher-local gadgets with unproven reductions), and keeps the paper's transformation classes and decision-problem framing.
decomposition_rationale: The source record explicitly separates this locality-reduction question from the transformation-class question; each is an independent research target with its own acceptance standard, so the record is split along that source-supported boundary. The ar5iv digit renderings (333/666/222) are preserved verbatim in the excerpt; the canonical statement uses the original 3/6/2 values as documented in the record's surrounding context.
rationale: The authors' NP-completeness proofs are confined to 3- and 6-local constructions, and they name the reduction to 2-local building blocks as an explicitly interesting open direction; the candidate restates exactly that target.

source_records.content: What is the computational complexity of deciding whether a k-local non-stoquastic Hamiltonian can be cured (transformed into a stoquastic, sign-problem-free form) by a constant-depth quantum circuit that also allows two-qubit rotations, whether discrete or continuous — and can the NP-completeness of finding curing transformations, proven for 3-local and 6-local Hamiltonians under single-qubit Clifford or orthogonal rotations, be extended to 2-local Hamiltonians?
source_records.paper_title: On the Computational Complexity of Curing the Sign Problem
source_records.exact_excerpt: It is important to clarify the computational complexity of finding the curing transformation in the case of constant-depth circuits that also allow two-body rotations, whether discrete or continuous.
source_records.surrounding_context: Marvian, Lidar and Hen prove that deciding whether a local Hamiltonian can be cured (made stoquastic, hence sign-problem-free for quantum Monte Carlo) is NP-complete when the allowed transformations are tensor products of single-qubit Clifford gates (3-local Hamiltonians, Theorem 1) or general single-qubit orthogonal matrices (6-local Hamiltonians, Theorem 2). In their 'Conclusions and open questions' section they state: 'It is important to clarify the computational complexity of finding the curing transformation in the case of constant-depth circuits that also allow two-body rotations, whether discrete or continuous. Also, since our NP-completeness proof involved 333 and 666-local Hamiltonians, it is interesting to try to reduce it to 222-local building blocks.' They further ask whether quantum algorithms can cure the sign problem more efficiently than classical ones, and conclude: 'We leave these as open questions to be addressed in future studies.' The 333/666/222 digit forms are ar5iv renderings of 3, 6, and 2 in the original text.

source_records.source_intent: The authors aim to re-found stoquasticity in complexity-theoretic terms ('computational stoquasticity'): after proving NP-completeness of curing under restricted single-qubit transformation classes, they explicitly flag richer transformation classes (constant-depth circuits with two-body rotations), lower locality (2-local), approximate curing (small positive off-diagonal elements), and quantum curing algorithms as unresolved extensions of their hardness results.
source_records.derivation_rationale: The proposed question restates the authors' own explicitly listed open questions without strengthening them: the hardness results are proven only for single-qubit transformation groups and 3-/6-local constructions, so the complexity of curing under constant-depth circuits with two-body rotations and for 2-local Hamiltonians is genuinely undecided by the paper. The question keeps the paper's decision-problem framing (does a curing transformation exist and how hard is it to find), which yields an unambiguous acceptance standard: a complexity classification (membership/hardness proof, algorithm, or counterexample) for the stated transformation class and locality.

evidence.supports: Direct: full HTML text inspected, including Theorems 1-2 (NP-completeness of curing under single-qubit Clifford and orthogonal transformations) and the explicit open-questions list quoted in the excerpt.
